A-setup.name: Setup refund-full scenario creates CAPTURED Payment
A-setup.description: GET /api/payments/evidence-setup?scenario=refund-full creates a Payment already in CAPTURED state with capture ledger Dr/Cr pair (2 entries).

B-refund-request.name: Request refund → returns REFUND_PENDING + creates reversal Dr/Cr
B-refund-request.description: POST /api/payments/refund creates Refund (REFUND_PENDING) + reversal Dr CONSUMER_REVENUE + Cr GATEWAY_RECEIVABLE inside ONE txn (atomic). Ledger total = 4 (2 capture + 2 reversal).

C-verify-pending.name: Verify state after refund request (Payment CAPTURED, Ledger=4, balanced)
C-verify-pending.description: After refund request, Payment is STILL CAPTURED (not REFUNDED yet), Ledger has exactly 4 entries (2 capture + 2 reversal), Dr sum == Cr sum (I-06 preserved), Refund is REFUND_PENDING.

D-publisher-fail.name: Publisher fail (simulateFail=true) → refund called, error returned, state unchanged
D-publisher-fail.description: POST /api/payments/evidence-publisher-run?refundId=X&mode=refund&simulateFail=true calls refundRazorpayPayment() OUTSIDE any txn (TRANSACTION_RETRY_INVARIANT preserved), returns SIMULATED_FAILURE error. Payment stays CAPTURED, Refund stays REFUND_PENDING. No new ledger entries (no duplicate).

E-verify-after-fail.name: Verify state after fail (Payment CAPTURED unchanged, Ledger=4 no duplicate, balanced)
E-verify-after-fail.description: After publisher failure, Payment status is STILL CAPTURED (unchanged), Ledger has exactly 4 entries (no duplicate from publisher retry), ledger still balanced. Refund still REFUND_PENDING. This proves the Option A pending ledger semantics: reversal entries persist as accounting reservation.

F-publisher-retry.name: Publisher retry (no simulateFail) → refund called, Refund → REFUNDED, Payment → REFUNDED
F-publisher-retry.description: POST /api/payments/evidence-publisher-run?refundId=X&mode=refund (no simulateFail) calls refundRazorpayPayment() OUTSIDE any txn. On success: Refund transitions REFUND_PENDING → REFUNDED, Payment transitions CAPTURED → REFUNDED (full refund). No idempotency skip (retry calls refund — Refund was in REFUND_PENDING, not REFUNDED).

G-verify-final.name: Verify final state (Payment REFUNDED, Ledger=4 no duplicate, balanced, no orphan)
G-verify-final.description: Final state: Payment REFUNDED, Refund REFUNDED, Ledger exactly 4 entries (NO duplicate from retry — Option A pending ledger semantics: reversal entries become canonical on success), Dr sum == Cr sum (I-06 preserved), no orphan ledger entries, PAYMENT_REFUNDED audit log exists, Outbox event PUBLISHED.

postgresqlDirectVerification.description: Direct SQL queries via Supabase Management API (https://api.supabase.com/v1/projects/$PROJECT_REF/database/query) — bypasses the app layer and confirms the same state is durable in PostgreSQL.

invariant.description: Wave-5 5a-E6 (Option A — Pending Ledger Semantics): Refund reversal entries are written at REFUND_PENDING time as accounting reservation (atomic with Refund + AuditLog + Outbox). On publisher failure, they persist as pending reservation (Payment stays CAPTURED, ledger balanced). On retry success, they become canonical — NO new ledger entries are created (no duplication). Dr sum == Cr sum invariant holds at ALL times (pending, failed, refunded).

accountingSemantics.design: Option A — Pending ledger semantics: reversal entries are created at REFUND_PENDING time as accounting reservation. On refund success, they become canonical (no new entries needed). On refund failure, they remain as pending reservation (Payment stays CAPTURED, ledger is still balanced).
accountingSemantics.invariant: Dr sum == Cr sum at ALL times (pending, failed, and refunded states).

governance.note: Wave-5 Sub-Wave 5a-E6 evidence: refund failure / pending ledger semantics verified on staging PostgreSQL. realPayments=false (demo mode — refundRazorpayPayment returns mock success; simulateFail=true forces SIMULATED_FAILURE error). No production traffic touched. Test data cleaned up.
